query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing ~10 vol % of a hybrid solid-lubricant dispersion consisting of silver and calcium-fluoride (Ag + CaF2) into an equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix will form temperature-adaptive tribofilms (Ag-rich shear layers below ≈400 °C and CaF2-derived fluoride layers above ≈400 °C). These in-situ regenerated films will keep the steady-state coefficient of friction ≤0.30 and lower the specific wear rate by ≥50 % compared with the unmodified CoCrFeNi over the entire 25–800 °C range during dry-air sliding.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, vacuum-induction–melted and homogenized (annealed 1100 °C, 2 h), fully f.c.c. polycrystalline bulk coupon or thick coating (HV≈200–250).
generation.intervention: Disperse 10 ± 2 vol % Ag + CaF2 (1:1 volume ratio, 1–3 µm particles) into the CoCrFeNi powder and consolidate by spark-plasma sintering (1000 °C, 50 MPa, 5 min) to obtain a dense (≥99 %) Ag/CaF2-reinforced HEA composite with randomly distributed, insoluble lubricant islands.
generation.conditions: Reciprocating or pin-on-disk sliding against an alumina ball, 5 N normal load, 0.1 m s⁻¹, 10 000 cycles, ambient laboratory air (RH 20–40 %), temperature steps at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Discrete Ag and CaF2 particles embedded in the f.c.c. CoCrFeNi matrix that can be pulled out, smear, soften, and react to form surface/transfer films rich in Ag and Ca–F–O compounds.
generation.mechanism: 1) 25–≈400 °C: ductile Ag spreads along the contact, forming a low-shear metallic film that accommodates plastic strain and blocks adhesive junctions. 2) ≥≈400 °C: CaF2 undergoes super-plastic flow and/or partial decomposition, releasing CaF2 (and Ca–O–F) layers with very low shear strength that protect both surfaces; residual Ag promotes heat dissipation and maintains electrical/thermal continuity, accelerating film self-repair. The HEA matrix supplies hardness and thermal stability, sustaining debris comminution without severe oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Across 25–800 °C: (i) steady-state coefficient of friction μ ≤ 0.30 (baseline CoCrFeNi: μ ≈0.5–0.8, rising sharply above 600 °C); (ii) specific wear rate K ≤ 2 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ at all temperatures (≥50 % lower than baseline at RT and ≥80 % lower above 600 °C); (iii) hardness loss of composite ≤10 % relative to starting HEA after high-temperature exposure.
generation.baseline: As-received CoCrFeNi HEA without lubricant phase, tested under identical conditions, showing μ ≈0.4 at RT increasing to ≥0.7 at 800 °C and wear rates of 4–10 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹.
generation.boundary: Efficacy expected in dry or mildly humid air; not guaranteed in vacuum (Ag effectiveness drops) or in moisture >60 % RH (CaF2 hydrolysis). Temperatures above ~900 °C (near CaF2 melting and significant HEA softening) or contact stresses >1.5 GPa may negate the benefit.
generation.uncertainty: Potential challenges include non-uniform dispersion or agglomeration of CaF2, silver loss by oxidation/sublimation above 700 °C, and unforeseen chemical interactions between fluoride and Cr/Fe oxides that could embrittle the surface.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: (A) baseline CoCrFeNi and (B) CoCrFeNi +10 vol % Ag–CaF2 composite (processing route as described). Conduct identical pin-on-disk tests at 25, 200, 400, 600, 800 °C (5 N load, 0.1 m s⁻¹, alumina counterface, air). Record real-time friction. Post-test, measure wear track cross-section by 3D profilometry and analyse tribofilms by XPS/EDS and TEM.
measurements: Specific wear rate (K) from wear volume
Hardness of subsurface region after test
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, at any test temperature, sample B shows (i) steady-state μ >0.35 OR (ii) wear-rate reduction <20 % compared with sample A, OR (iii) absence of Ag- or F-containing tribofilm on the wear track.
